The source photo has arms raised; this legs-only variation keeps both arms resting, with the left forearm comfortably supported. The photo is a leg-pattern reference, not the prescribed arm position.

form_cues: Unlike the photo and full demo, keep both arms resting; support the left forearm comfortably.
Move only the legs; no reaching, squeezing, or pressing with the injured arm.
Keep your ribs and pelvis steady while breathing normally; shorten the leg reach if your back arches.
Count one leg extension as one rep; alternate sides evenly.
notes: Legs-only regression of the dead bug. The linked guide describes moving the legs alone as a regression, while its video demonstrates the full arm-and-leg exercise. Follow these supported-arm instructions; this is not forearm rehabilitation.
instructions: Use a mat only if you can get down and back up safely without pushing, gripping, or bearing weight through the left arm. Otherwise skip this exercise.

Lie on your back. Rest both arms comfortably, supporting the left forearm on a cushion or beside your torso. Do not copy the raised arms in the photo or the arm reach in the video; do not force the elbow straight or rotate the palm up.
Bring bent knees above the hips with shins roughly parallel to the floor. Keep the ribs and pelvis steady and breathe normally.
Slowly reach one leg away only as far as you can without arching your lower back or bracing through your arms. Return that leg, then repeat with the other; a smaller reach is fine.
Each leg extension counts as one rep; alternate sides evenly. Stop if arm symptoms appear, then lower the feet and use your planned exit without pushing through the left hand or elbow.
